subject: SET statement (value in NaN payload)
notes: DOCUMENTED (kb/Work PB452, 2026-09-09) IN THE SAME CHANGE SET AS THE GENERAL RULES IT RIDES. A.1 item 176 is a REQUIRED documentation obligation on 14.9.39.4 GR34 and GR35 - the NaN PAYLOAD a SET CONTENT OF ... TO FLOAT-NOT-A-NUMBER / FLOAT-NOT-A-NUMBER-SIGNALING stores - and it had no row while the general rules themselves had no implementation at all; a required implementor-definition with no documentation row is not 'implemented'. The determination: payload ZERO for the quiet form and ONE for the signaling form, giving binary32 0x7FC00000 / 0x7F800001 and binary64 0x7FF8000000000000 / 0x7FF0000000000001, with the sign bit set from GR34/GR35's own SIGN phrase and positive when the phrase is absent. Zero is the canonical NaN every IEEE implementation produces; one is the smallest payload that keeps the significand nonzero once ISO/IEC 60559:2020 6.2.1's quiet bit is cleared, which a signaling NaN requires. 14.9.39.3 SR32 confines the receiver to a STANDARD floating-point usage and the two WiseOwl COBOL provides are binary32 and binary64 EXACTLY, so the basic interchange format the rules name IS the carrier. The values are emitted as BIT PATTERNS through BitConverter, never as a CLR constant: double.NaN carries a SET sign bit, so the positive default would otherwise be spelled -double.NaN and depend on constant folding, and the CLR has no signaling-NaN constant at all because every managed arithmetic path quiets one. IeeeSpecials is one table serving as both the documented encoding and the emitted one, and IeeeSpecialsTests asserts the two agree by DECODING them rather than string-matching. The COBOL-observable witness can see that a NaN is unequal to itself but not which kind it is: the class condition that would expose the distinction (8.8.4.4's FLOAT-NOT-A-NUMBER-QUIET / -SIGNALING) is kb/Work PB225 and unimplemented. kb/Work/PB961 (2026-09-22): RE-RECORDED ON THE STORED IMAGE. The prior CONFORMS rested on the emitted EXPRESSION (unit:IeeeSpecialsTests.TheEmittedExpression_EvaluatesToTheDocumentedBits), while the pipeline stored a binary32 signaling NaN as the QUIET 0x7FC00001 - the JIT carried the inline BitConverter constant as a double, and the binary32 image lane widened through double. The value now reaches the item through CobolFloat.FromBinary32Bits (opaque to the JIT) and CobolNum.FormatImageSingle/ParseImageSingle (no binary64), and a same-usage MOVE copies on the carrier (14.9.25.4 GR6 c)). Witness: conformance:cases/14.9.39-SET/pb961_signaling_nan_binary32 reads 0x7F800001 = 2139095041 back through a BINARY-LONG UNSIGNED REDEFINES and asks GR3 k) of every copy; unit:IeeeSpecialsTests.TheStoredImage_CarriesTheDocumentedBits follows the emitted text to the stored image in both byte orders. IeeeSpecials.Text is deleted (Bits is the one table; RuntimeApi.FloatFromBits spells it). docs/CONFORMANCE.md DOC-A.1-176 corrected in the same change set (the "cannot quiet the value" sentence was true of the expression and false of the pipeline). retired-witness: src/Cobol.Net.Compiler/Binding/IeeeSpecials.cs#Text (IeeeSpecials.Text was deleted by kb/Work PB961 (the emitted expression is RuntimeApi.FloatFromBits over IeeeSpecials.Bits) and TheEmittedExpression_EvaluatesToTheDocumentedBits was replaced by TheStoredImage_CarriesTheDocumentedBits, which asserts the stored image rather than the expression) retired-witness: unit:IeeeSpecialsTests.TheEmittedExpression_EvaluatesToTheDocumentedBits (IeeeSpecials.Text was deleted by kb/Work PB961 (the emitted expression is RuntimeApi.FloatFromBits over IeeeSpecials.Bits) and TheEmittedExpression_EvaluatesToTheDocumentedBits was replaced by TheStoredImage_CarriesTheDocumentedBits, which asserts the stored image rather than the expression)
